AccountChange.description: One account a transaction changed: its state before and after.

balanceBefore.description:
Balance in wei before and after, decimal strings. Absent when the account did not
exist on that side — never `"0"`.

codeHashBefore.description:
Code hash before and after, `0x`-prefixed (the hash of empty code for an account
without code). Absent when the account did not exist on that side.

existedBefore.description:
The account existed before the transaction. `false` means every `…Before` field is
absent.

existsAfter.description:
The account exists after the transaction. `false` (destroyed) means every `…After`
field is absent.

nonceBefore.description: Nonce before and after. Absent when the account did not exist on that side.

storageDestroyed.description: The account's storage was wiped by the transaction.

AccountStateChange.description:
What one block changed in the account: the net change over the whole block, not per
transaction.

balanceBefore.description:
Balance in wei before and after the block, decimal strings. `balanceBefore` is absent
when the account did not exist before — never `"0"`.

balanceChanged.description: Which parts changed in the block.

codeHashBefore.description: Code hash before and after, `0x`-prefixed. Absent on a side where it is not recorded.

created.description:
The account did not exist before this block: a first receipt of ETH, a first EIP-7702
delegation, or a deployment. Every `…Before` field is then absent.

nonceBefore.description: Nonce before and after the block. `nonceBefore` is absent with `balanceBefore`.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds.

ActivityBySource.description:
The newest block each activity source saw the address at. A key is never omitted:
`null` means the source was consulted and holds nothing for this address.

calls.description:
Calls the address RECEIVED: it was the target of a call inside a transaction —
with or without value, reverted or not. What says a contract is in use when it is
only ever called by other contracts.

directTx.description: Top-level transactions from or to this address.

internalTransfers.description: Value-bearing call frames the address took part in.

tokenTransfers.description: Token transfers with this address as sender or receiver.

referenceBlock.description:
Block height at which the attribute was evaluated. Per attribute: different
attributes of the same address can be proven at different heights.

result.description: Evaluation result. `pass` means the attribute is proven for this address.

AttributeHistory.description: Every attribute interval an address has held, oldest first.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coveredFamilies.description:
Attribute families the history is built for. An empty or short timeline says
nothing about attributes of other families. Intervals of the `behavior` family state
an observed pattern, not a verdict; the most recent of them are evaluated again as
later blocks arrive and may shorten or disappear.

intervals.description:
Intervals in ascending order of `startBlock`, then attribute id. An interval with
no `endBlock` was still open at the end of the covered history.

truncated.description:
`true` when the timeline was cut at `limit`: what is listed is a prefix of the
address's history, not the whole of it.

AttributeInterval.description: One attribute and the block window it held for.

attributeId.description:
Attribute id, `family:name` — the same vocabulary as the current attributes, which
is what makes "was it true then" comparable with "is it true now".

endBlock.description:
Last block the attribute held at. Absent when the interval was still open at the
end of the covered history: an end that was not observed is not stated.

startBlock.description: First block the attribute held at.

value.description: The attribute's value over the interval, for attributes that carry one.

AttributesAtBlock.description:
The attributes an address held at one block.

Answered from the interval history, which covers the families listed in
`coveredFamilies` only. An attribute of another family is never listed here, whether or
not it held — compare with the current attributes method for those.

addressKnown.description:
`false` when the address is unknown to the history altogether — a different answer
from an empty `intervals` ("known, nothing proven at this block"). Absent when the
history does not state it.

block.description:
The block the question was asked about, echoed so a forwarded answer cannot be
mistaken for another block's.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coverageBlock.description:
The highest block the history has been computed up to. `block` is at or below it;
a question past it is refused with `block_not_available`.

coveredAttributeIds.description:
Single attribute ids with a history although their family is not in
`coveredFamilies`.

coveredFamilies.description:
Attribute families the history is built for, whole. With `coveredAttributeIds` it
says what this answer can list: an attribute is covered when its family is here or
its id is there. Any other attribute is not listed whether or not it held, so its
absence says nothing about it. `behavior` is here only when `block` is at or below
the height that family has been computed to, which can trail `coverageBlock`.

intervals.description: The attributes that held at `block`, each with its window.

AuthorityStatus.description: Whether the signer of an authorization is known.

Authorization.description:
One entry of an EIP-7702 authorization list: an account's signed permission for its
code to be delegated to a contract.

address.description: The contract the account delegates its code to, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

authority.description:
The account that signed the authorization — the account whose code is delegated —
lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Present only when `authorityStatus` is `recovered`.

authorityStatus.description:
What is known about the signer: `recovered` (`authority` names it),
`recovery_failed` (the signature is not valid, so the authorization has no signer
and does not take effect), or `not_available` (not determined yet — retry later;
this is not a statement that there is no signer).

chainId.description: The chain id the authorization was signed for; `0` means any chain.

index.description: Position of the entry inside that transaction's authorization list, from `0`.

nonce.description: The signing account's nonce at the time of signing.

txHash.description:
Hash of the transaction that carried this authorization, lowercase and
`0x`-prefixed.

txIndex.description: Position of that transaction inside the block, from `0`.

txNumber.description:
Sequence number of the transaction that carried this authorization, counted across
the whole chain. Orders the block's transactions; the position inside the block is
`txIndex`.

yParity.description: The signature: recovery bit, and the `r` / `s` components as `0x`-prefixed hex.

BalanceHistory.description: Daily history of an address's native balance.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

granularity.description: Granularity of `points`. `day` is the only value served.

points.description:
One point per day on which the balance changed, oldest first, at most `limit`
of the most recent such days.

BalancePoint.description: The native balance of an address at the end of one day.

balanceWei.description: Balance at the end of the day, in wei, decimal string.

blockNumber.description: The last block of that day in which the balance changed.

changeWei.description: Net change over the day, in wei, decimal string; negative when the balance fell.

timestamp.description: Start of the day, Unix seconds, UTC.

txCount.description:
Blocks in which the balance changed that day. Despite the name it is not a number
of transactions: several transactions of one block count once, and a change made by
an internal call or a block reward counts too.

oneOf.description:
USD value at the day's close. Absent for the current, unfinished day and for days
without a price.

BalancePointUsd.description: USD value of a balance point at the day's close.

priceCarried.description: `true` when no price was observed in that hour and the latest earlier price is used.

priceHour.description: Start of the UTC hour the price is for (the day's last hour), Unix seconds.

priceUsd.description: USD price of one ETH at `priceHour`.

firstActivityTimestamp.description:
First and last account-state change of the address ever, Unix seconds — not
limited to the window. Absent when the address never changed account state.

startBalanceWei.description: Balance before the first point: the first point's balance minus its change.

totalInflowWei.description:
Sum of the NET daily changes of the days whose balance rose, wei. Not the gross amount
received: ether that arrived and left within one day cancels out inside that day's
net change and is not counted. For gross movement read the address's transactions
and internal transfers.

totalOutflowWei.description:
Sum of the net daily changes of the days whose balance fell, wei, as a positive
number. Not the gross amount sent, for the same reason.

totalTxCount.description:
Sum of the points' `txCount`: blocks in which the balance changed, over the window —
not a number of transactions.

BalanceWindow.description: The block a balance answer is true at.

asOfBlock.description:
The block the answer is true at — the state at the END of that block. With
`kind: block`, the requested block itself. With `kind: current`, the block the
current TOKEN balances are valid at.

oneOf.description:
Present (`head`) on a current portfolio: the native asset's balance is read up to the
chain head, so it can be newer than `asOfBlock`, which the token balances are valid
at. Absent when every position is at `asOfBlock`.

BalanceWindowKind.description: Which state a balance answer describes.

BeaconImplementations.description: What a beacon handed to its proxies over time.

completeThroughBlock.description:
The history is complete AT LEAST through this block — a lower bound shared by every
beacon; a change after it may not be listed yet. Absent when `not_proven` or not
stated.

implementations.description:
Newest first; the first entry without `endBlock` is what the beacon hands out now.
Empty when `not_proven`.

provenFromBlock.description:
First block the history vouches for. Before it, nothing is stated. Absent when
`not_proven`.

BeaconPeriod.description: One period of a beacon's implementation.

endBlock.description:
Last block it did, INCLUSIVE — the next period starts one block later. Absent for the
current one. Same names and convention as `endBlock` in the attribute and relation
histories; the producer's exclusive end is converted here (platform-documents, 22.10).

startBlock.description: First block the beacon handed out this implementation at (end of block).

BlacklistEnforcement.description:
Enforcements one issuer recorded against the address: funds destroyed or frozen. A
separate fact from membership — an enforcement neither lists nor unlists.

count.description: How many enforcement events the issuer recorded against the address.

issuerContract.description: The contract that enforced, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

oneOf.description:
The most recent enforcement — present only when it is also the issuer's most recent
event about the address of any kind. Every enforcement is listed by the events
method.

tokenSymbol.description: The issuer's token symbol when it is a token contract with one; absent otherwise.

BlacklistEnforcementEvent.description: The last enforcement an issuer recorded against the address.

blockNumber.description: Block height.

eventName.description:
The event's name as the issuer's contract declares it (`DestroyedBlackFunds`,
`FundsFrozen`, …).

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

BlacklistEvent.description: One blacklist event an issuer contract recorded about the address.

authorityTier.description:
The issuer's weight: `recognized_issuer`, `arbitrary_token` or `unknown`. Absent
when it cannot be stated.

blockNumber.description: Block height.

eventName.description: The event's name as the issuer's contract declares it.

issuerContract.description: The contract that emitted it, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

logIndex.description:
The event's log index within the block. With `blockNumber` it identifies the
event: one transaction can emit the same event twice.

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

txHash.description: The transaction that emitted the event, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

BlacklistEvents.description:
One page of the blacklist events about an address, newest first.

Facts recorded on-chain by the issuer contracts themselves (blacklist / unblacklist /
enforcement events); no external sanctions lists.

address.description: The address asked about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

events.description:
Newest first. Empty when no issuer ever recorded an event about the address — a
fact as of `meta.asOfBlock`.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

BlacklistFeed.description: One page of every blacklist event on the chain, newest first.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one.

BlacklistFeedEvent.description:
One event of the chain-wide blacklist feed: an issuer contract listed, unlisted or enforced
against an address.

address.description: The address the event is about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

authorityTier.description:
The issuer's weight: `recognized_issuer`, `arbitrary_token` or `unknown`. Absent when it
cannot be stated as one value.

blockNumber.description: Block height.

eventName.description: The event's name as the issuer's contract declares it.

issuerContract.description: The contract that emitted it, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

logIndex.description: The event's log index within the block. With `blockNumber` it identifies the event.

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

txHash.description: The transaction that emitted the event, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

BlacklistFeedResponse.description: Response of the chain-wide blacklist feed.

BlacklistIssuer.description: One issuer contract and how many addresses its list holds.

authorityTier.description:
The issuer's weight: `recognized_issuer`, `arbitrary_token` or `unknown`. Absent when
the issuer's records do not state one value.

enforced.description: Addresses it enforced against (funds destroyed or frozen).

everListed.description: Addresses it has a recorded listing (`add`) of, including those it removed again.

issuerContract.description: The contract that keeps the list, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

tokenSymbol.description: The issuer's token symbol when it is a token contract with one; absent otherwise.

BlacklistIssuers.description: The issuer contracts that keep blacklists, most addresses listed first.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

issuerCount.description: Issuer contracts with any blacklist record.

issuers.description: The top `limit` issuers by `currentlyListed`, ties by contract address ascending.

listedAddresses.description: Distinct addresses some issuer lists now.

listedPairs.description: (address, issuer) pairs listed now — an address listed by two issuers counts twice.

BlacklistIssuersResponse.description: Response of the blacklist issuers method.

BlacklistListing.description:
One issuer contract's blacklist and where this address stands in it.

Facts recorded on-chain by the issuer contracts themselves (blacklist / unblacklist /
enforcement events); no external sanctions lists.

authorityTier.description:
How much weight the issuer carries: `recognized_issuer` (a curated stablecoin or
asset issuer), `arbitrary_token` (any other token contract that emits blacklist
events) or `unknown` (a contract nothing further is known about). A listing by an
arbitrary token is that token's own decision and says nothing beyond it.

firstListedBlock.description:
The block in which the issuer first listed the address. Absent when it cannot be
stated.

issuerContract.description:
The contract that keeps the list, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Usually a token
contract with a freeze or blacklist function.

lastAction.description:
The issuer's latest membership transition about the address: `add` (listed) or
`remove` (unlisted).

lastEventBlock.description:
The block of the issuer's most recent event about the address, of ANY kind —
`lastEventKind` says whether it was a membership transition or an enforcement.

lastEventName.description:
The event's name as the issuer's contract declares it (`AddedBlackList`,
`Blacklisted`, `DestroyedBlackFunds`, …).

lastEventTimestamp.description: Unix time of that event, seconds.

lastEventTxHash.description: The transaction that emitted it, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

listCount.description: How many times the issuer listed the address.

listed.description:
`true` while the issuer's list currently holds the address; `false` after the issuer
removed it.

tokenSymbol.description:
The issuer's token symbol (`USDT`, `USDC`, …) when the issuer is a token contract
with one; absent otherwise.

unlistCount.description: How many times the issuer removed it again.

BlacklistStatus.description:
Which issuer contracts list one address, and which have enforced against it.

Facts recorded on-chain by the issuer contracts themselves (blacklist / unblacklist /
enforcement events); no external sanctions lists. There is deliberately no single
"blacklisted" verdict: a listing is one issuer's decision, weighted by its
`authorityTier`, and the reader decides what it means.

address.description: The address asked about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

enforcement.description: Every issuer that enforced against the address, one row each. Empty when none did.

listedBy.description:
Every issuer that ever listed the address, one row each, currently listed or not.
Empty when no issuer ever did — a fact as of `meta.asOfBlock`.

BlacklistedPair.description: One address an issuer contract lists now.

authorityTier.description:
The issuer's weight: `recognized_issuer`, `arbitrary_token` or `unknown` — the same
value `getBlacklistIssuers` states for the issuer. Absent when the issuer's records do not
state one value.

enforcementCount.description: How many times the issuer enforced against the address (funds destroyed or frozen).

firstListedBlock.description: The block in which the issuer first listed the address. Absent when it cannot be stated.

issuerContract.description: The contract that lists it, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

lastEventBlock.description:
The block of the issuer's most recent event about the address, of ANY kind —
`lastEventKind` says which. Not the start of the current listing.

lastEventLogIndex.description: Its log index within the block; present only beside `lastEventTxHash`.

lastEventName.description: The event's name as the issuer's contract declares it.

lastEventTimestamp.description: Unix time of that event, seconds.

lastEventTxHash.description: The transaction that emitted it, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when unknown.

BlacklistedPairs.description: One page of the (address, issuer) pairs listed now, in address order.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one.

pairs.description: The pairs, by address and then issuer contract, ascending.

Block.description: One Ethereum block: its header and the totals of what it contains.

baseFeePerGas.description: Base fee per gas in wei, decimal string. Absent before EIP-1559.

blobBaseFeeWei.description: Blob base fee in wei for this block, decimal string. Absent before Cancun.

blobGasUsed.description: Blob gas used and excess blob gas (EIP-4844), decimal strings. Absent before Cancun.

burntFees.description:
Fees: burnt base fees (absent before EIP-1559), total gas fees paid, total priority
fees (tips) — wei, decimal strings.

contractCreationCount.description: Transactions that created a contract, and EIP-4844 blob transactions.

difficulty.description:
Header `difficulty` as a decimal string (`"0"` since the merge), and `extraData`,
`0x`-prefixed.

feeRecipient.description: The address that received the block's priority fees (the header's `beneficiary`).

gasLimit.description: Gas limit and gas used, as decimal strings.

logCount.description:
Number of receipt logs across all transactions. Absent with the two outcome counts
when the block's receipt aggregates were not computed.

ommersCount.description: Number of ommers (0 since the merge).

stateRoot.description: State root after this block, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

successfulTxCount.description:
Absent, together with its two siblings, when the block's receipt aggregates were
not computed — never zero there, because a block with transactions cannot
have no outcomes. Absence is "not stated", never "none".

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

totalGasFees.description:
Total gas fees the block's transactions paid, and the part that went to the
proposer as tips. Absent TOGETHER when they were not computed — never a
zero fee for a block that ran transactions, and never a negative tip.

totalValueWei.description: Sum of transaction values in wei, decimal string.

txCount.description: Number of transactions, and how many of them succeeded / failed.

uniqueAddressCount.description:
Distinct addresses whose state the block touched. Absent for the most recent
blocks while the count is still being reconciled — absence is "not yet counted",
never zero.

withdrawalCount.description:
Validator withdrawals in this block, and their total in gwei (decimal string).
The count is ABSENT for the most recent blocks while it is not available
for them — absence is "not stated", never zero; the total is always stated.

BlockAddress.description: One account whose own state changed in a block.

afterBalanceWei.description: Native balance at the end of the block, in wei as a decimal string.

balanceChanged.description:
What changed: the native balance, the nonce, the code; and whether the account was
created in this block.

beforeBalanceWei.description:
Native balance before the block, in wei as a decimal string. Absent when the account
had no prior state (created in this block) — never zero in its place.

BlockAddresses.description: A page of the accounts whose own state changed in one block.

addressCount.description: How many accounts the block touched in total.

addresses.description: This page, in address order. An account appears once per block whatever it did.

blockNumber.description: The block these accounts were touched in.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for.

BlockAtTime.description: The bracket of blocks around a moment.

block.description: The last block whose time is at or before `timestamp`.

final.description: `true` once a block after `timestamp` exists: no later block can land at or before it.

oneOf.description: The first block after `timestamp`. Absent while no such block exists yet.

timestamp.description: The time asked about, Unix seconds.

BlockAuthorizations.description: A page of one block's EIP-7702 authorizations.

authorizations.description:
This page, in transaction order and then list order. Empty when the block carries no
type-4 transaction.

blockNumber.description: The block these authorizations belong to.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for.

BlockInternalTransferRow.description: One call frame that moved ETH.

callDepth.description: Depth in the call tree: 2 = called by the transaction's target.

callType.description: `call`, `callcode`, `create`, `create2` or `selfdestruct`. Other values may be added.

status.description:
`success`, `revert` or `halt` — the frame's own outcome. A successful frame inside a
reverted transaction, or under a reverted parent frame, moved nothing in the end.

to.description: The receiving account. Absent where the frame names none.

txSender.description:
Who sent the transaction — not necessarily `from`, which is the frame's sender
(often a contract). Absent when not resolved.

BlockInternalTransfers.description: The internal ETH transfers of one block, in transaction order.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

total.description: How many rows the block has in all.

BlockInternalTransfersResponse.description: Response of the block internal-transfers method.

BlockParticipantRow.description: One address's part in a block.

accountChanged.description: Its own account changed in the block.

blockPhase.description: `pre_tx`, `tx` or `post_tx` — where in the block it took part. Absent when not known.

firstTxIndex.description:
The first transaction it took part in. Absent when it took part only outside
transactions.

nature.description: What the address was at the block, when `natureState` is `known`.

natureState.description:
`known`, `unclassified` (computed, no class holds — a fact, not a gap), `not_computed`
(the knowledge graph has not reached this block; says nothing about the address) or
`unavailable` (could not be read; retry).

primaryClass.description:
The one class the address is counted under in the block, strongest first:
`initiator`, `tx_recipient`, `call`, `token`, `event`, `protocol`, `state`.

roles.description:
Every role the address had in the block: `state` (its own account changed),
`system_call`, `tx_sender`, `tx_recipient`, `call_caller`, `call_callee`, `created`,
`token_party`, `log_emitter`, `withdrawal`, `auth_delegate`, `fee_recipient`,
`topic_address` (named in an event), `auth_signer`. Other values may be added.

oneOf.description:
The change: balances before and after in wei, and the signed delta (present only when
both sides are). Absent when the account did not change.

tokenFlows.description:
Its token transfers in the block, summed per token, raw units. Absent when the block's
token transfers were not summed for this answer.

txCount.description: How many of the block's transactions it took part in.

BlockParticipants.description: Every address one block touched, in the block's order, with the block's counts.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

outsideTxCount.description:
Of them, the ones that took part only outside transactions (system calls,
withdrawals, the fee recipient).

participantCount.description: Every address that took part in the block.

stateChangedCount.description: Of them, the ones whose own account changed.

tokenFlowsComputed.description:
`false` when the token transfers of the block could not be summed for this answer:
then `tokenFlows` is absent on every row and says nothing. Absent when not stated.

total.description: How many rows there are to page through.

BlockParticipantsResponse.description: Response of the block participants method.

BlockRef.description: A block's number and its time.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds.

tokenStandard.description: `erc20`, `erc721` or `erc1155`. Other values may be added.

BlockTokenTransfer.description: One token transfer event of a block: which token, and the transfer.

BlockTokenTransfers.description: The token transfers of one block, in transaction and log order.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

total.description: How many rows the block has in all.

BlockTokenTransfersResponse.description: Response of the block token-transfers method.

BlockTransactions.description: A page of one block's transactions.

blockNumber.description: The block these transactions belong to.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for.

txCount.description: How many transactions the block holds in total.

BlockWithdrawal.description: One validator withdrawal paid out in a block.

amountGwei.description: The amount, in gwei (1 gwei = 10^9 wei), as a decimal string.

index.description:
The withdrawal's index — a counter that runs across the whole chain, so it is unique
and increases from block to block.

validatorIndex.description: Index of the validator the withdrawal was paid for, in the consensus-layer registry.

BlockWithdrawals.description: A page of one block's validator withdrawals.

blockNumber.description: The block these withdrawals belong to.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for, filters
included.

withdrawalCount.description:
How many withdrawals of the block match the request — the block's whole count when
no filter is given. A block before the withdrawals upgrade holds none.

CallSpan.description: The first and the last block in which an address received a call.

CapabilityFact.description: One fact as the knowledge graph states it.

referenceBlock.description: The block the fact was evaluated at.

result.description: `pass` (proven). Other values may appear and are not proof.

value.description:
The value, for a fact that has one (for example the signature threshold of a
Safe in `capability:safe_threshold_current`), as a JSON scalar in text. Absent
otherwise.

CodeClone.description: One contract running the shared code.

blockNumber.description: Block height at which this contract's code was set.

CodeMetadataRange.description: The compiler's metadata at the end of a contract's code: data, not instructions.

CodeTarget.description: Which code a code-analysis answer is about, and how it was reached from the address.

codeAddress.description: The address whose code this is, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

resolvedVia.description:
How the code that runs at the address was found at the block: `own` (its own code),
`slot` (a proxy's implementation slot), `beacon` (a beacon proxy's beacon),
`beacon_unproven` (a beacon whose implementation is not proven at the block), `eip1167`
(a minimal proxy's target), `delegate` (an EIP-7702 delegation).

targetUnresolved.description:
Present (`true`) only when `auto` found no proven code to follow and the address's own
code is served instead.

ConsensusAddressValidator.description: One validator whose withdrawals go to an address.

effectiveBalanceGwei.description: Effective balance in gwei, decimal string.

status.description: The beacon chain's status as of the snapshot.

ConsensusAddressValidators.description:
The validators that direct their withdrawals to an address, as of the validator snapshot.
The address is where the payouts GO — not the owner or the operator.

The execution-layer address the validator's withdrawals are paid to, lowercase and
`0x`-prefixed. Absent when its withdrawal credential names no address. Never the
block's fee recipient, which is usually a builder or a relay — a different party.

ConsensusProposerAddress.description:
One withdrawal address in the block-proposal leaderboard: the proposals of every
validator whose withdrawals are paid there, summed.

A withdrawal address is the destination of payouts, not evidence of ownership or
operation: the largest on mainnet is a staking pool's vault funded by unrelated
depositors. Nothing here claims an operator.

The block-proposal leaderboard for a window, in one of two groupings.

Both groupings are served because they rank different sets: the leading validator
proposes a handful of blocks per week, while the leading withdrawal address sums
thousands over thousands of validators. Collapsing the per-validator list by address
would not produce the address ranking; ask for it instead.

distinctProposers.description: Distinct validators that proposed in the window.

Only when grouped by address: blocks whose proposer has no withdrawal address, so
no address can claim them. Reported as a count rather than bucketed under a
placeholder address.

validators.description: The ranking, when grouped by validator. Absent otherwise.

executionBlockNumber.description: Execution block of the newest proposed published slot. Absent when none is known.

ConsensusQueueAverages.description:
Trailing averages of the two queue depths. Each is absent (`null`) until the observed
series spans its window; a value here is a mean over the epochs of the window.

pendingActivation7d.description: Mean activation-queue depth over the last 7 days, in validators.

pendingExit30d.description: Mean exit-queue depth over the last 30 days, in validators.

pendingExit7d.description: Mean exit-queue depth over the last 7 days, in validators.

ConsensusQueueChurn.description:
The per-epoch churn limits of the Electra rules, gwei, decimal strings: the balance the
chain lets through each epoch on each side.

activationExitGweiPerEpoch.description: The budget deposits and exits each get per epoch.

consolidationGweiPerEpoch.description: The budget consolidations get per epoch.

ConsensusQueueFlow.description:
Validator flow that landed in blocks over trailing windows — exits (voluntary and
execution-layer requested, summed) and deposits. Flow, not queue depth. A value is
`null` while the window has not been computed.

deposits30d.description: Deposits that landed in the last 30 days.

exits24h.description: Validators that exited in the last 24 hours.

exits30d.description: Validators that exited in the last 30 days.

exits7d.description: Validators that exited in the last 7 days.

ConsensusQueueGap.description:
The span between the end of the reconstruction and the start of sampling, which no
series covers. Draw a break, not a line: a missing span is not an empty queue.

from.description: Start of the uncovered span, RFC 3339 UTC.

to.description: End of the uncovered span, RFC 3339 UTC.

ConsensusQueuePoint.description:
One point of the queue timeline: the closing sample of its day.

`source` says which of two series the point comes from. `observed` points are sampled
from the live chain, one per day at the day's last sampled epoch; their `queues` is
`null` on days before the Electra queues began to be sampled. `reconstructed` points
predate observation and are a lower-bound estimate of the STATUS counts at roughly
1.14-day resolution, derived from validator activations and exits — a queue that
drained faster than that reads as 0 there; the reconstruction ends at the Electra fork
(2025-05-07), and what it cannot know is `null`, never estimated.

epoch.description: The sampled epoch (`observed`) or the estimate's boundary epoch (`reconstructed`).

oneOf.description:
The queues by the Electra rules, with churn and wait estimates in epochs. `null`
where not sampled.

time.description: Time of the sample, RFC 3339 UTC.

totalActiveBalanceGwei.description:
Total effective balance of the active set, gwei, decimal string. `null` on
`reconstructed`.

ConsensusQueueSet.description:
The validator queues by the Electra rules, read from the beacon state's own pending
lists. Since Electra a validator's STATUS no longer says whether it is queued: deposits
wait as balances rather than as pending validators, and the exiting set also holds
consolidation sources. These are the queues; `status` beside them keeps the status-set
counts.

oneOf.description: The whole active set — active, exiting and slashed — and its actual balance.
Pending consolidations; `gwei` is the balance of their source validators.
The deposit queue, new validators and top-ups.
Validators exiting, consolidation sources excluded — the exit queue.

Validators already out of the active set, waiting to become withdrawable. Not a
queue a validator joins.
Pending partial withdrawals and their amount.

Entries on this side (deposits, requests or validators — named by the field holding
it).

ConsensusQueueState.description:
The queue state the series is headed by — the same facts as the current method, cut
down to what a chart needs beside its newest point.

oneOf.description:
The queues by the Electra rules, with churn and wait estimates. `null` if the
sample predates their measurement.

The capital weight of one validator status set at the registry snapshot. Two sums over
the same validators: effective balances and actual balances.

effectiveGwei.description: Sum of their effective balances, gwei, decimal string.

validators.description: Validators in the status set at the snapshot.

The capital weight of the two status sets (pending activation, exiting), with the
freshness of the registry snapshot it was taken from. A status set is not the queue
since Electra — for the queues and their wait estimates read `queues`. The registry is
sampled daily while the counters beside it move every epoch, so the snapshot age is
part of the fact.

oneOf.description: Validators pending activation. Absent when the snapshot holds none.
Validators in the exiting status. Absent when the snapshot holds none.

snapshotAgeEpochs.description: How many epochs the snapshot trails `asOfEpoch`.

ConsensusQueues.description:
The validator queues as a summary: the current state plus a bounded daily series,
newest first.

The series is cut to the most recent `limit` days out of the last 90: one closing point
per UTC day, observed where sampling had begun and reconstructed before that (see
`ConsensusQueuePoint.source`); on the day sampling began the observed close stands for

grain and over longer windows, is not published here.

The span of the 90-day window between the end of the reconstruction and the start of
sampling, when the window reaches into it. Only that span: a pause of sampling itself
is not listed here.

granularity.description: Always `day`: one point per UTC day.

observedFrom.description:
When sampling of the queues began, RFC 3339 UTC. Points before it are
`reconstructed`. `null` while nothing has been sampled yet.

depth.description: Slots rolled back. Absent when the event did not carry it.

executionBlockNumber.description:

yet or holds no block. It is never guessed.

newHeadRoot.description: Beacon root of the new head and of the head it replaced, `0x`-prefixed.

reconstructed later.

ConsensusSlotResponse.description: Response of the consensus slot method.

Validator counts by STATUS. Before Electra these were the queues; since Electra they are
not (`pendingActivation` holds a few hundred validators while the deposit queue holds
over a million ETH, and `pendingExit` includes consolidation sources). Served under this
name so that no reader mistakes them for the queues in `queues`.

activeOngoing.description:
Validators in the `active_ongoing` status — exiting and slashed ones excluded. The
whole active set is `queues.activeSet`. `null` on `reconstructed` points.

pendingActivationGwei.description:
Actual balance of the pending-activation set, gwei, decimal string. `null` when not
sampled.

Validators in an exiting status (exit queue, consolidation sources and validators
already out of the active set).

The epoch of the snapshot the card is taken from. The snapshot is taken about once a

The validator's status as of `snapshotEpoch`, as the beacon chain names it

The execution address the validator's payouts go to. It is a DESTINATION, not the

withdrawalCredentials.description:
The 32-byte withdrawal credentials, `0x`-prefixed. The public key and the credentials

complete; misses are a lower bound — assignments are recorded from slot 14 971 296

How long each queue takes to drain at the current churn: queue balance divided by the
per-epoch limit (the entry queue is also bounded by 16 deposits an epoch). ESTIMATES of the queue as a whole, not a promise to any one
validator: they ignore finality and deposit-inclusion delays and move with the queue.

entryDays.description: The entry estimate in days. Stated on the current state only.

waits.

Contract.description: One deployed contract: what its code is, what it looks like, and how it came to be.

blockNumber.description: Block height of the current code record.

bytecodeSize.description: Size of the current runtime code in bytes.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

oneOf.description:
Opcode-level facts of the current code. Absent with `proxyFamily`: absent is not
"none found".

codeHash.description: Keccak-256 hash of the current runtime code, `0x`-prefixed.

isEip1167Proxy.description: `true` when the bytecode is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy.

isErc20.description:
`true` when the bytecode exposes all four ERC-20 view functions; see
`erc20Interface` for each one.

oneOf.description: Deployment and destruction, when the lifecycle index has reached the address.

proxyConfidence.description: Confidence of `proxyFamily`, 0 (none) to 3 (high). Absent with it.

proxyFamily.description:
Proxy pattern detected from this contract's own bytecode, for example
`minimal_proxy`, `eip1967_impl`, `beacon`, `storage_delegate` (the code delegates to an
address it reads from storage), `eip7702` (an account delegated by EIP-7702),
`diamond_like`; `none` when no pattern was recognised, `unknown` when the analysis was
inconclusive. The set grows as patterns are added. A classification of the code, not
of a pointer: it can differ from `proxyFamily` on the proxy method's rows. Absent when
the code has not been analysed for it.

proxyImplementation.description:
The implementation an EIP-1167 proxy delegates to. Absent otherwise; the proxy
method lists implementations of every proxy kind.

selectorCount.description:
Number of 4-byte selectors found as constants in the code: the contract's own
functions, the selectors of functions it calls on other contracts and its custom
errors together. Not the number of its functions.

ContractBytecode.description: The runtime bytecode of a contract.

bytecode.description:
The runtime code, `0x`-prefixed hex. Up to 24 576 bytes of code, i.e. up to 49 154
characters. Empty when the code is not stored for this hash.

bytecodeSize.description: Size of the code in bytes.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

fingerprint.description:
A structural fingerprint of the code that is stable across metadata-only
differences, `0x`-prefixed. Two contracts with equal fingerprints share their logic.

ContractCapabilities.description: What a contract can do, by power, as the knowledge graph proves it.

capabilities.description:
One entry per power with at least one proven answer, by name: `mint`, `burn`,
`pause`, `blacklist`, `freeze`, `seize`, `upgrade`, `emergency_withdraw`, … Other
names may appear.

graphReached.description:
`true` when the knowledge graph holds any fact about the address — not that it has
evaluated every power. Either way an absent answer means "not proven"; `false` says
that nothing at all is known yet.

otherFacts.description:
Other proven capability facts of the address that are not one of the three questions,
as the knowledge graph names them (for example `capability:currently_paused`,
`capability:mint_permissionless`, `capability:permit_supported`).

ContractCapability.description:
Three questions about one power. An answer is present only when it is proven; an absent
answer is "not proven", never "no".

oneOf.description: The power can be used right now.
The code exposes the power.
The power has been used on chain.

ContractClones.description: The contracts that run exactly the same runtime code as one contract.

address.description: The contract asked about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

codeHash.description:
Keccak-256 hash of its current runtime code, `0x`-prefixed: what every listed contract
shares.

contractCount.description: How many contracts the list holds in all, across every page.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

ContractCodeFeatures.description: What the analysis of a contract's current code found at the opcode level.

delegatecallTargetFromStorage.description:
A DELEGATECALL target is read from storage, shown by following the data flow: the code
the contract runs can be changed by writing that storage slot, which is how upgradeable
proxies work. `true` is proven; `false` only when the code has no DELEGATECALL at all.
Absent when the code has a DELEGATECALL and no storage-held target was proven — not
proven is not "none". An account delegated by EIP-7702 (`proxyFamily: eip7702`) runs
its delegate's code without any of these opcodes: its features describe the 23-byte
delegation, not that code.

hasCallcode.description: The code contains CALLCODE, the deprecated predecessor of DELEGATECALL.

hasDelegatecall.description:
The code contains DELEGATECALL: it can run another contract's code against its own
storage and balance.

ContractControlHistory.description: The writes to a proxy's control slots, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

ContractCreation.description: One contract creation: a successful CREATE or CREATE2 frame.

blockNumber.description: The block of the creation.

codeHash.description:
Keccak-256 hash of the code this creation deployed, `0x`-prefixed. Absent on a
`rolled_back` row, and on a `committed` one when it cannot be stated for this creation
yet — absent is not "no code".

isEip1167Proxy.description:
Whether that code is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy. Absent with `codeHash`; absent is not
`false`.

originAddress.description:
The account that signed the creating transaction — the deploying wallet when the
creator is a factory.

outcome.description:
`committed`: the creation took effect. `rolled_back`: the creating frame succeeded but
a frame above it or the transaction failed, so no contract came from this row.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds. Absent when not known.

ContractDecompilation.description: A contract's code reconstructed as readable pseudocode.

address.description: The address asked about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

block.description: The block the code was resolved at.

disclaimer.description: Read this before relying on the view.

functionCount.description: Entries of the table of contents, on every answer.

releaseIsCurrent.description:
`false` when the view was made by an earlier analysis release and is served while the
current release's view is computed.

status.description:
`done`, `partial`, `unsupported` or `failed`; for a day after an attempt that could not
finish, `timeout_wall`, `timeout_cpu` or `failed_infra` (retried after that). With no
view behind the status, `functions` is empty and `functionCount` is 0.

ContractDisassembly.description: A contract's code as instructions, a page at a time.

address.description: The address asked about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

block.description: The block the code was resolved at.

instructionCount.description: Instructions in the whole code, every page together.

instructions.description: The page's instructions, in pc order.

oneOf.description: The compiler's metadata at the end of the code; absent when the code has none.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

ContractEvents.description: One page of the events a contract emitted.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

ContractFunctionCalls.description: Calls per function of an address.

oneOf.description:
First and last block in which the address received ANY call, calls from inside other
contracts included. Absent with `callSpanAsOfBlock` present: no call up to that block.

callSpanAsOfBlock.description:
The block `callSpan` is stated up to. Absent when it cannot be read right now — then
nothing is said about the span either way.

coverage.description:
`top_level_only`: the counts cover transactions sent TO the address; calls made from
inside other contracts are not counted.

entryCount.description: Entries in this answer, the `no_selector` entry included.

truncated.description:
Present (`true`) only when the address received more selectors than one answer
lists (1 000); the least called are left out.

ContractFunctionCallsResponse.description: Response of the contract function-calls method.

ContractHotSlots.description: The storage slots of a contract that changed in the most blocks of a recent window.

lastChangeBlock.description: Only with an empty window: the contract's newest change before it, when known.

slots.description: At most 25, by the number of blocks they changed in; ties by key.

totalSlotsInWindow.description: How many slots changed in the window in all — `slots` is the top of this set.

windowFromBlock.description: The window, inclusive on both ends.

ContractHotSlotsResponse.description: Response of the hot slots method.

ContractIdentity.description:
The identity of a contract: which code it runs, how to recognise that code elsewhere, and
how the contract came to be.

bytecodeSize.description: Size of the current runtime code in bytes.

codeHash.description: Keccak-256 hash of the current runtime code, `0x`-prefixed (the EXTCODEHASH).

fingerprint.description:
A structural fingerprint of the code that is stable across metadata-only differences,
`0x`-prefixed: two contracts with equal fingerprints share their logic. Absent when
the code is not stored, and for an EIP-7702 delegation (as `runtimeSha256`).

oneOf.description:
Deployment, code changes and self-destruction, when the lifecycle index has reached the
address.

runtimeSha256.description:
SHA-256 of the same code, `0x`-prefixed — the hash Sourcify and other verifiers look
code up by. Absent when it is not recorded for this code, and for an account delegated
by EIP-7702 (`bytecodeVariant: eip7702`), whose 23 bytes are a delegation, not code.

ContractLifecycle.description: How the contract came to exist and whether it still does.

codeChangeCount.description: Number of code states observed, deployment included.

deployBlock.description: Block the contract was deployed at.

deployCodeHash.description: Hash of the code deployed at `deployBlock`.

deployTxHash.description: Hash of the creating transaction. Absent when the creation frame is not indexed yet.

deployTxIndex.description: Index of the creating transaction within its block.

deployer.description:
The account that executed the creation — a factory, or the sender itself. Absent
when the creation frame is not indexed yet.

latestCodeBlock.description:
Block of the latest code change observed (equal to `deployBlock` when the code never
changed).

latestCodeHash.description:
Hash of the code at `latestCodeBlock` (equal to `deployCodeHash` when the code never
changed). Absent when the lifecycle index does not state it.

origin.description:
The externally-owned account that sent the creating transaction. Absent when the
creation frame is not indexed yet.

selfDestructBlock.description: Block the contract self-destructed at; absent while it is alive.

ContractSecurity.description: The security profile of a contract's code: how it is built and how it can change.

architecture.description:
What the knowledge graph proves about how the contract is built, as it names it — for
example `architecture:immutable`, `architecture:upgradeable_proxy`,
`architecture:has_mutable_impl_slot`, `architecture:metamorphic`,
`architecture:minimal_proxy_eip1167`. Only proven facts are listed; an absent one is
"not proven", never "no".

oneOf.description: Opcode-level facts of the code. Absent with `proxyFamily`.

codeHash.description: Keccak-256 hash of the current runtime code, `0x`-prefixed — the code described here.

graphReached.description:
`true` when the knowledge graph has reached the address at all; `false` means an
empty `architecture` says nothing about the contract.

proxyConfidence.description: Confidence of `proxyFamily`, 0 (none) to 3 (high). Absent with it.

proxyFamily.description:
Proxy pattern detected in the code (the vocabulary of `proxyFamily` on the contract
method). Absent when the code has not been analysed yet.

ContractSelectors.description:
The 4-byte selectors found as constants in a contract's bytecode: its functions, the
selectors it calls on other contracts and its custom errors, not told apart.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

codeHash.description: Keccak-256 hash of the code the selectors were read from, `0x`-prefixed.

selectorCount.description:
Number of selectors in `selectors` — functions, called selectors and custom errors
together, not the number of the contract's functions.

selectors.description: The selectors, each with its resolution.

ContractSlotHistory.description: How one storage slot of a contract changed, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

readThroughBlock.description: The newest block this page was read through.

ContractSlotHistoryResponse.description: Response of the slot history method.

ContractStorageActivity.description: How a contract's storage was read and written, per UTC day.

fromDate.description: The window, UTC dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive; `toDate` is partial.

readThroughBlock.description: The block the last day holds the blocks through.

series.description: Oldest first; only days with activity.

ContractStorageActivityResponse.description: Response of the storage activity method.

ContractStorageParameters.description: The direct storage slots of a contract with their current values.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

readThroughBlock.description: The block the list was read through.

ContractStorageParametersResponse.description: Response of the storage parameters method.

ContractStorageProfile.description: Totals of a contract's storage writes over its history.

delegatecallWrites.description: Writes that ran through DELEGATECALL, and their share of all writes (percent, 0–100).

firstWriteBlock.description: The first and last block a write happened in.

maxCallDepth.description: The deepest call depth a write happened at.

uniqueSlots.description:
Distinct slots, callers and executing code addresses among them — estimates on large
contracts.

ContractStorageProfileResponse.description: Response of the storage profile method.

ContractStorageWriters.description: Who writes a contract's storage, ranked by writes.

totalPairs.description: How many (caller, execution address) pairs wrote its storage in all.

ContractStorageWritersResponse.description: Response of the storage writers method.

ControlChange.description: One write to a proxy's control slot.

blockNumber.description: The block, the transaction's index in it and its hash.

callerAddress.description: Who called the frame that wrote the slot, and whose code ran in it.

kind.description:
`upgrade` (a value written), `unset` (written to zero) or `cleared` (wiped with the
account). Other values may be added.

newValue.description: The value written (all zeros on a `cleared` row).

oldValue.description:
The slot's value before the write, 32-byte hex. All zeros means the slot was empty
before — not necessarily a first deployment. Absent when it cannot be stated.

slot.description:
The slot: `eip1967_impl` (implementation), `eip1967_admin` (admin), `beacon`,
`oz_v1` (the older OpenZeppelin implementation slot) or `safe_singleton` (a Safe's
master copy). Other values may be added.

CorpusBasis.description: How the `corpus` figure beside a ranking was obtained.

Counterparty.description: One counterparty of the ranked address.

firstBlock.description: First and last block the two interacted in, within the window.

interactionTxCount.description: All transactions between the two, attempts included (reverted ones too).

receivedTxCount.description: Transactions in which the ranked address is the receiving side, by the same rule.

sentTxCount.description:
Transactions in which the ranked address is the sending side of an interaction with
the counterparty: it sent the top-level transaction (ETH or not), or it is the `from`
of an internal ETH transfer or of a token `Transfer` event. NOT the transactions it
signed: an event naming it as `from` counts here whoever emitted it.

succeededTxCount.description: The ranking key: transactions between the two that succeeded.

surfaceCounts.description:
Transactions per surface, for exactly the surfaces listed in `surfaces`. On the
attempts scale (like `interactionTxCount`), and a transaction touching two surfaces
counts on both — so the values explain where the relation lives, and do not add up to
the ranking key. Absent when the source of this answer does not carry the breakdown
(high-degree addresses served from the pre-built top list); absence means the
breakdown was not computed, never zero.

propertyNames.description: Where an interaction can be observed.

surfaces.description:
On which surfaces the relation was observed: `external` (top-level transactions),
`internal` (calls inside transactions), `token` (token transfers). A surface missing
here had no interaction between the two.

tokenClasses.description:
Which classes of token the `token` surface consists of: `fungible`, `nft`, or both.
Present only when `surfaces` includes `token`. Both listed means the relation spans
both classes; it does not say in what proportion.

CounterpartyRanking.description: The addresses one address interacts with most, ranked.

address.description: The address the ranking is about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

boundaryTieCount.description:
How many counterparties are level with the LAST row served and did not make the list.
Zero means nothing ties with the boundary. Ties are common — at the
hundredth place of a mid-sized address there are typically hundreds of equals — which
is also why rows carry no rank number: the order is all the data supports.

corpus.description:
How many distinct counterparties the ranking covered — the size of the set the list
is the top of. A list of 100 out of a `corpus` of 216 770 is a different statement
from 100 out of 104.

oneOf.description: How `corpus` was obtained. See `CorpusBasis`.

counterparties.description:
In ranking order: most successful transactions first, then most recent, then by
address. At most `limit` rows; no rank number (see `boundaryTieCount`).

window.description: What the ranking covers: the whole history, or the state at the end of a block.

asOfBlock.description:
The block the ranking is true as of. For `all`, the block the relationship graph
was last built to; for `block`, the requested block.

kind.description:
`all` — the whole history up to `asOfBlock`; `block` — everything up to and
including the requested block.

DailyActivity.description:
Per-day account-state activity of an address over a window ending at the latest day
the daily aggregate holds.

activeDays.description: Days in the window with at least one active block.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

days.description: Length of the window in days.

points.description: One entry per ACTIVE day, oldest first. A day with no activity has no entry.

DailyActivityPoint.description: One day of an address's activity.

balanceChangeBlocks.description: Of those, blocks with a balance change.

blocksActive.description: Blocks in which the address's account state changed that day.

codeChangeBlocks.description: Of those, blocks with a code change.

createdBlocks.description: Of those, blocks in which the account was created.

nonceChangeBlocks.description: Of those, blocks with a nonce change (transactions sent).

value.description:
The value: addresses as `0x` strings, integers as decimal strings, bytes as `0x`
hex, booleans as booleans. An indexed dynamic argument (string, bytes, array) is
only its hash on chain and is returned as `{ "hash": "0x…", "dynamic": true }`.

DecodedEvent.description: A decoded event: its name and arguments.

candidateCount.description:
How many known signatures fit this log: share its hash and decode its topics and
data. `1` is unambiguous.

DecompilationAnalysis.description: What a decompiled view is and when it was made.

codeHash.description: Keccak-256 hash of the decompiled code, `0x`-prefixed.

computedAt.description: When the view was computed, RFC 3339 UTC.

release.description:
The analysis release that produced the view, `rev:` + 12 hex. Opaque: compare it,
never parse it.

DecompiledArgument.description: One argument of a decompiled function.

type.description: The type the code checks; absent where the code does not fix one.

DecompiledBody.description: The decompiled body of one function.

text.description: The function as Solidity-like pseudocode, with known names filled in.

DecompiledFunction.description: One entry of a decompiled view's table of contents.

bodyOmitted.description:
Present (`true`) only when the body was left out to keep the view within its size
limit.

candidateCount.description: How many known signatures share the selector.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the name is: `partial` (one known signature), `ambiguous` (several
share the selector), `abi_missing` (none known). Absent when no lookup was made.

hasBody.description: Whether `?selector=` returns a body for this entry.

lowConfidence.description: The reconstruction of this function is uncertain.

mutability.description: State mutability where the code shows it, for example `view` or `payable`.

name.description: The function name, when a known signature has this selector.

status.description: How far this function's analysis got: `done`, `partial`, `timeout`, `failed`.

DelegatedCodeStatus.description: Whether the response states the code EIP-7702 delegated accounts ran.

resolvedThroughBlock.description: The highest block for which delegated code is decided.

status.description:
`resolved`: every frame into an account with a delegation carries
`executedCodeAddress`, so a frame without it ran its own code. `pending`: not
decided yet for this block (a recent one) — no frame carries it, and its absence says
nothing; ask again later.

DexTrade.description: One swap on a DEX pool.

logIndex.description: The swap event's index in the block.

poolAddress.description:
The pool's address. Absent for a pool that has no address of its own (Uniswap V4):
`poolId` identifies it.

poolId.description:
The pool's own 32-byte id where it has one (the Uniswap v4 PoolId, as the protocol's
events name it). Absent for a pool with an address, and for a v4 pool TraceFast's pool
registry has not caught up with yet.

priceCarried.description:
`true` when the price behind `valueUsd` was carried from an earlier hour (nothing priced
the token in the trade's hour); `false` when it was observed in that hour. Absent with
`valueUsd`.

protocol.description:
The venue and its version as the index names them, for example `uniswap` / `v3`,
`curve`, `sushiswap`. Other values may be added.

role.description:
This address's part: `sender` (it sent the swap), `recipient` (it received the
output), or `sender_and_recipient`.

sender.description:
The swap's sender and recipient as the pool's event states them. The sender is often a
router; some venues state no recipient.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds.

tokenIn.description:
The token sold into the pool and the token bought from it, with the raw amounts in
each token's smallest unit (decimal strings), its decimals and its own on-chain symbol
where known. A symbol is the token's claim about itself, not a verification.

valueUsd.description:
Estimated USD value of the trade at the hour it happened: the bought amount × that
token's price for the hour (observed in it, or carried from an earlier hour — see
`priceCarried`), or the sold amount when the bought token has no usable
price. Absent when neither leg can be valued — including a leg larger than its price's
market can vouch for, which is left unvalued, never capped.

valuedLeg.description: Which leg `valueUsd` is of: `out` (bought) or `in` (sold). Absent with it.

Eip7702Delegation.description: Whether an account delegates its code with EIP-7702, to whom and since when.

coveredThroughBlock.description:
The block the account's delegation history is guaranteed complete through. Delegations
AFTER it may already be included — in `delegate` / `sinceBlock` and in the two counts —
but are not promised to be all there yet; `none` is stated only up to this block.
Absent with `unknown`.

delegate.description:
With `delegated`: the contract the account's code points at, lowercase and
`0x`-prefixed.

delegationCount.description: How many delegations the account has made in all, and to how many distinct contracts.

sinceBlock.description:
With `delegated`: the block this delegation began. With `revoked`: the block the last
one ended.

state.description:
`delegated` — it delegates now; `revoked` — it did, and no longer does; `none` — it
never has, as far as `coveredThroughBlock`; `unknown` — this could not be determined
right now (not a statement that it never delegated).

EntityActivity.description:
When an address was first mentioned, when its own account state last changed, and
when it was last active in any form.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

firstSeenBlock.description:
The first block that mentions this address anywhere on chain. Absent when it could
not be resolved.

oneOf.description:
The newest block at which the address was active in any form, with the sources
consulted. This is the field to read as "last active".

lastInteractionBlock.description:
The newest top-level transaction with this address as sender or recipient. Absent
when none was observed.

lastStateChangeBlock.description:
The last block at which the address's OWN account state (balance, nonce, code)
changed. For a contract that is only ever called this is its deployment. `null` for
an address whose account state was never touched.

stateChangeCount.description:
Number of account-state changes observed. `0` is entailed for an address whose
account state was never touched.

EntityAttributes.description: Facts proven for one address by the TraceFast knowledge graph.

attributeDetails.description: One entry per id in `attributes`, in the same order, with the evaluation detail.

attributes.description:
Attribute ids proven for this address, in `family:name` form
(for example `address_nature:eoa_currently`, `address_presence:tx_sender_ever`).
Empty when nothing is proven yet — absence of an attribute never means its opposite.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

oneOf.description:
Provisional classification, present while the knowledge graph has not yet reached
this address. See `TypeHints`.

EntityAttributesResponse.description:
Response of the address-attributes method: the facts under `data`, response metadata
under `meta`.

EntityCallsReceived.description: The transactions that called an address, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

EntityDeployments.description: The contract creations an address made, oldest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

EntityDexTrades.description: The DEX trades an address took part in, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

EntityDexTradesResponse.description: Response of the DEX trades method.

EntityInternalTransfers.description: A page of an address's internal transfers, newest first.

EntityOverview.description: One address as the chain currently sees it.

accountType.description:
`eoa` (an externally owned account) or `contract` (code present). An account that
delegates its code with EIP-7702 is `eoa`: its only code is the delegation designator.
For a `storage_only` address `eoa` is entailed: an account that was never touched
never held code.

balanceWei.description: Native balance in wei, decimal string. `0` is entailed for a `storage_only` address.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

createdAtBlock.description:
Block the account was created at (first account-state change). Absent for a
`storage_only` address.

directTxCount.description:
Top-level transactions with this address as sender or recipient. A contract reached
through another contract is almost absent from this count: read it as "direct
transactions", never as usage.

oneOf.description:
The account's EIP-7702 delegation, for an account that is not a contract. Absent on a
contract (a contract cannot delegate).

existenceKind.description:
How the address exists on chain: `account` (its balance, nonce or code was touched at
least once) or `storage_only` (it is mentioned by chain operations — a token transfer
party, a call target — but its account state was never touched: no balance, no
nonce, no code, ever).

firstSeenBlock.description:
The first block that mentions this address anywhere on chain. Absent when it could
not be resolved — never `0`.

lastActiveBlock.description:
The newest block at which the address was active in ANY form: a top-level
transaction, a token transfer, an emitted log, a value-bearing call. `null` only when
nothing was observed on any source; see the activity method for the breakdown.

lastActiveTimestamp.description:
Unix time of `lastActiveBlock`, seconds. `null` when the block is `null` or its
instant could not be resolved.

lastInteractionBlock.description:
The newest top-level transaction with this address as sender or recipient. Absent
when no such transaction was observed — a contract reached only through other
contracts has none.

nonce.description: Transaction count of the account (its nonce).

receivedTxCount.description: Top-level transactions addressed to this address.

sentTxCount.description: Top-level transactions sent by this address.

totalFeesPaidWei.description: Fees paid by the transactions this address sent, in wei, decimal string.

txStatsAsOfBlock.description:
The block the transaction counters were last computed at. Absent when they are
entailed zeros (no direct transaction was ever observed).

EntityResolution.description:
What a reference — an address, a name, a token symbol or name — resolves to: the
addresses it can mean, best first, each with what TraceFast shows for it and what kind of
address it is.

oneOf.description:
For a query that is a whole number: the block with that number, when TraceFast holds
it. Absent when it does not — a number past the chain head, or a block in a range that
is temporarily unavailable: absence is not "no such block". The same query is also
looked up as text (a token can be named by digits).

chainId.description: Chain id the matches are on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

hasMore.description:
`true` when more addresses matched than were returned: ask with a larger `limit`, or
a more specific query. There is no cursor.

matches.description:
Best first, by whose name it is, then by how closely it matched. First the addresses
TraceFast presents as verified; then projects, exchanges, protocols and ENS names
TraceFast knows by name — flagged ones included, since a sanctioned protocol is still
the protocol asked for; then everything else that is not flagged, such as tokens known
only by what they declare about themselves; last, addresses flagged as imitating an
asset or flagged without a known name — shown, never hidden. Inside each group: exact,
then prefix, then substring, then a match only inside a text carrying an address-like
hex string; then tokens with more holders; then the shorter matching text. Empty when
nothing matched.

query.description: The query as it was looked up: trimmed of surrounding whitespace.

queryKind.description:
`address` when the query is an address (`0x` + 40 hex) — the one match is that
address, described — or `text`, looked up by name and by token symbol and name.

searched.description:
The collections a `text` query was looked up in: `tokens` (token contracts by the
symbol and name they declare) and `names` (the names TraceFast shows for projects,
exchanges, protocols and ENS names). A collection missing from this list was not
consulted for this answer, so no match in it means nothing. Absent for an address.

oneOf.description:
For a `hash` query: the transaction with that hash, when TraceFast knows one. A
32-byte hash is looked up as a TRANSACTION only — a block hash is not resolved here
(look a block up by its number). Absent when no transaction has that hash.

EntityStateChanges.description: The blocks that changed one account's own state, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

EntityTokenTransfers.description: A page of an address's token transfers, newest first.

EntityTransactions.description: A page of an address's transactions, newest first.

address.description: The address this feed is about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

Erc20Interface.description: Which ERC-20 view functions the bytecode exposes, from its selectors.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code — one of the closed set in the documentation
(`bad_request`, `not_found`, `chain_not_supported`, `method_not_allowed`,
`uri_too_long`, `block_not_available`, `portfolio_too_large`, `token_not_covered`,
`balance_not_available`, `service_unavailable`, `internal_error`). Branch on this
and on `details.reason`, never on the sentence.

details.description:
Present only when the refusal carries something to act on: `reason` (a stable
sub-code), the bound that was hit and the actual value. Absent otherwise.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation. Numbers a client must act on are also given in
`details`; do not parse them out of this sentence, it may be reworded.

requestId.description:
The request's id, echoed from the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it when asking for
support: it identifies this exact call. Absent only when the request did not carry
one.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response. Every refusal, whichever layer raises it, has this shape.

EventLog.description: One event log emitted by a transaction, with its decoding when the signature is known.

address.description: The contract that emitted the log, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

blockNumber.description: Block, transaction index within the block, and the log's index within the block.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the decoding is: `verified` (one known signature, decoded), `partial`,
`ambiguous` (several known signatures fit this log; `decoded` is the best candidate),
`inferred`, `abi_missing` (signature unknown), `failed` (the signature is known but
none of its known layouts fits this log's topics and data — the log is served raw,
without `decoded`).

oneOf.description: The decoded event, when the signature is known and the data decodes.

logIndexInTx.description: The log's index within its transaction (emission order).

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

topics.description: The log's topics in order (`topics[0]` is the event signature hash), `0x`-prefixed.

txHash.description: Hash of the transaction that emitted the log, `0x`-prefixed.

EvidenceSource.description: One evidence source a proof was read from.

sourceId.description:
Opaque identifier of the evidence source, `ev:` + 12 hex characters. Stable: the
same source carries the same identifier in every proof, so sources can be told
apart and matched across proofs.

logIndexes.description:
Positions within the transaction's receipt of the logs this frame emitted,
ascending. Empty when it emitted none.

ExecutionFrame.description:
One frame of the paged, frame-level trace: the call frame as in the summary, with its
calldata and output heads always present, plus the event logs it emitted.

FailedFrame.description: One failed call frame inside a reverted transaction.

callDepth.description: Depth from the root frame, 1 = root.

callPath.description:
Position in the call tree: four hex characters per level, the root frame is
`0000`. Sort by `(callDepth, callPath)` to render the tree.

errorName.description:
Human-readable error name and canonical signature (for example `Error(string)`)
when the selector is known; both absent otherwise — render `revertSelector` then.

from.description: The frame's caller and target, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

revertData.description:
The revert payload, `0x`-prefixed; `0x` when the frame reverted with no data.
Capped at 4 KB: `revertDataTruncated` says when, and `revertDataLength` is the
full length.

revertSelector.description:
First four bytes of the revert payload, `0x`-prefixed (`0x00000000` when the
payload is shorter).

status.description: `Revert` (the frame reverted) or `Halt` (the EVM halted the frame).

FeedInternalTransfer.description:
One internal transfer: a value-carrying call frame inside a transaction. The
transaction's own top-level call is NOT one of these — it is the transaction, and it
rides the transactions feed.

callDepth.description:
Depth in the call tree; `1` is the transaction's own top-level call, which never
appears here.

callPath.description:
The frame's position in the call tree, as the trace encodes it — the third component
of this feed's cursor.

counterparty.description: The other party of the frame, when there is one.

to.description:
The frame's recipient. Absent where the trace records none — a `selfdestruct`

Assets the address holds a positive balance of that could NOT be valued: no USD price
