Proof.description:
The evidence behind one proven fact — an attribute of an address, or a relation
between two addresses. Nothing here is summarised or ranked: the fields are the
evaluator's own record, so a reader can check the claim rather than trust it.

bindingVersions.description:
The data bindings the evaluation read, keyed by an opaque binding identifier
(`ev:` + 12 hex characters). Each value is the version of what the binding was
resolved to — a plain version such as `1.0.0` where the evaluator recorded one,
otherwise an opaque identifier of the resolved source. Both identifiers are stable:
the same binding, and the same source, carry the same identifier in every proof.
Absent when the record does not state the bindings in a readable form.

chainId.description: Chain id the fact is about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

definitionVersion.description: Version of the definition the fact was evaluated against.

dependencyProofRefs.description:
Other proofs this one depends on. `null` when the record does not state them in a
readable form.

evaluatedAt.description: When the evaluation ran, Unix time in seconds.

evaluatorVersion.description:
Version of the evaluator that produced this proof, e.g. `1.0.0`. A different value
on two proofs means they were produced by different evaluator releases.

factResults.description:
The facts checked, each with its identifier (`fact_id`), the operator, the expected
and the observed value. Where a check names the evidence it read, that reference is
an opaque identifier (`ev:` + 12 hex characters), stable across proofs. `null` when
the record does not state the checks in a readable form.

failureReasonCodes.description:
Reason codes when `result` is not `pass`. Empty on a passing fact; `null` when the
record does not state them in a readable form.

graphRevision.description:
Revision of the knowledge graph's rule set that produced this proof: an opaque
identifier, `rev:` + 12 hex characters. Stable — the same revision carries the same
identifier in every proof; compare it for equality, it has no order.

negativeControlResults.description:
Conditions that had to be false for the fact to hold, each with its identifier
(`control_id`) and what was observed. `null` when the record does not state them in
a readable form.

object.description: The other end of a relation. Absent on an attribute proof.

proofHash.description: Digest of the proof record, `sha256:` + hex.

referenceBlock.description: Block the evidence was read at.

referenceBlockHash.description: Hash of that block, `0x`-prefixed — pins the evidence to one chain state.

result.description: Evaluation result. `pass` means the fact is proven.

selectedFamilyId.description: Which of the fact's alternative evidence families satisfied it.

snapshotId.description: Identifier of the chain snapshot the evaluation ran on.

sourceEvidenceRefs.description:
Where the evidence was read from: one entry per evidence source, each an opaque
identifier. Absent when the record does not state the sources in a readable form.

subject.description: The address the fact is about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

value.description: The fact's value, for facts that carry one.

ProofResponse.description: Response of the two proof methods.

ProvenAt.description: A proven answer and the block it speaks about.

referenceBlock.description: The block the answer was evaluated at.

ProxyImplementation.description: One implementation a proxy has been observed delegating to, and whether it still does.

oneOf.description:
Only on a `storage_beacon` row, where `implementation` is the BEACON: the logic
contracts the beacon handed to its proxies, read on the beacon itself. Absent on every
other row, and when the beacon's history could not be read.

firstSeenBlock.description: First and last block the pointer was observed at.

implementation.description:
The implementation address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. For a beacon proxy this is
the BEACON: the logic contract behind it is resolved on the beacon, not here.

isSelfDelegation.description: `true` when the proxy delegates to itself.

proxyFamily.description:
Pattern classification of the proxy contract, for example `eip1967_impl`, `beacon`,
`minimal_proxy`, `safe`; `none` or `unknown` when no pattern was recognised. The set
grows as patterns are added.

slot.description:
The storage slot the pointer was read from, `0x`-prefixed. Absent for
`eip1167`, where the pointer is in the code.

oneOf.description:
The last write observed on the pointer's slot: `upgrade` (a new implementation
was written), `cleared` (the slot was emptied) or `unset` (the pointer was removed:
zero written), with the block and transaction. Absent when no write to the slot is
indexed.

source.description:
How the implementation was found: `eip1167` (minimal-proxy bytecode),
`storage_eip1967_impl` (the EIP-1967 implementation slot), `storage_beacon` (the
EIP-1967 beacon slot), `storage_oz_v1` (the OpenZeppelin v1 slot),
`storage_safe_singleton` (slot 0 of a Safe proxy: the singleton it delegates to).

supersededBy.description:
Whether this pointer has since been replaced. Three states, and each means something
different: ABSENT — storage cannot say (the pointer lives in the code, or on a
beacon upgraded elsewhere); `null` — no replacement observed, the pointer is current;
an address — the pointer was replaced by it.

supersededByBlock.description: Block of the replacement. Present exactly when `supersededBy` is an address.

ProxyImplementations.description: The implementations a proxy contract has delegated to.

address.description: The proxy contract address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

implementations.description:
Newest-seen first. Empty when no implementation pointer has been observed for the
address — which is not a statement that it is not a proxy.

asOfBlock.description:
The block height the answer is valid at — the same place on every method, whatever
the body's own shape. Absent when the method's source states no block (a ranking
recomputed daily, a set of proven facts): absence means "not stated", never
"latest".

cached.description:
`true` when the answer came from the TraceFast response cache rather than being
computed for this call. Cached answers are refreshed within minutes.

chain.description: Network the answer is about. `ethereum` for chain id `1`.

coverage.description:
Block heights that bound what this method can state, by name — for example the
first block from which a derived fact is computed, or the last block a lagging fact
has reached. Present only on methods whose coverage is bounded; each such method
documents its keys. Re-read on every call, so a cached body carries current bounds.

docs.description: Documentation page of the method that produced this response.

timestamp.description: When this response was produced, Unix time in milliseconds.

ReceivedCall.description: One transaction that called the address — directly or from inside another contract.

blockNumber.description: The block and the transaction's index in it.

callTypes.description:
The kinds of those frames: `call` and `staticcall` (the address was called),
`delegatecall` and `callcode` (the address ran ANOTHER contract's code in its own
context, as a proxy does), `selfdestruct` (a self-destruct sent its balance here).
Other values may be added.

carriedValue.description: At least one of those frames carried ETH.

failedFrames.description: Of them, how many failed by themselves (reverted or halted).

frames.description:
How many call frames of the transaction ran in this address's context — on its own
storage and balance (counted up to 65 535). For a proxy this includes the frames in
which it ran its implementation's code, so one call to a proxy is often two frames.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds. Absent with `txHash`.

transactionTarget.description:
`true` when the address is the transaction's own target; `false` when it was called
only from inside other contracts.

txHash.description: The transaction's hash. Absent when it could not be resolved for this answer.

txSender.description:
The account that sent the transaction (not necessarily the direct caller: the call may
come from a contract it reached). Absent with `txHash`.

txSucceeded.description:
`false` when the transaction itself reverted: then nothing it did took effect, even if
`failedFrames` is 0 (a frame undone by its caller keeps its own success). Absent with
`txHash`.

counterpart.description:
The other end of the relation, lowercase `0x`-prefixed: the object when `direction`
is `subject`, the subject when it is `object`.

referenceBlock.description: Block height at which the relation was evaluated.

result.description: Evaluation result. `pass` means the relation is proven.

value.description: The relation's value, for relations that carry one.

RelationCount.description: How many addresses point at one address under one relation id.

count.description: Addresses holding this relation towards the address, now.

RelationHistory.description: Every relation interval an address has held, in one direction, oldest first.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coveredFamilies.description:
Relation ids the history is built for. An empty or short timeline says nothing
about relations outside this list.

direction.description:
The side the address is read on, echoed: `subject` lists what it pointed at,
`object` lists who pointed at it.

intervals.description: Intervals in ascending order of `startBlock`, then relation id, then the other end.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for.

total.description:
Number of intervals the address holds as the subject — the length of the whole
timeline under `direction=subject`. Absent under `direction=object`, which is not
counted.

truncated.description: `true` when the timeline was cut at `limit`; `nextCursor` continues it.

RelationInterval.description: One relation and the block window it held for.

counterpart.description:
The other end of the relation, lowercase `0x`-prefixed: the object when the
address is the subject, the subject when the address is the object.

endBlock.description:
Last block the relation held at. Absent when the interval was still open at the
end of the covered history.

startBlock.description: First block the relation held at.

value.description: The relation's value over the interval, for relations that carry one.

Relations.description: One page of the relations an address holds now.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

counts.description:
`direction=object`, first page only (no `cursor`): how many addresses point at this
one, per relation id, ordered by id; narrowed to `attributeId` when it is given.
Current as of the graph's latest hourly refresh — there is no single block for it,
it is a separate read from the page and may differ from it by one refresh, and
`meta.asOfBlock` does not describe it. An empty list means nothing proven points at
this address. Absent on the subject side and on later pages: not computed there,
never zero.

direction.description:
The side the address is read on, echoed: `subject` lists what it points at,
`object` lists who points at it.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page. There is no single total.

relations.description: The page, ordered by relation id then counterpart.

RelationsAtBlock.description: The relations an address was the subject of at one block.

address.description:
The address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Always the SUBJECT of the relations
listed: "what did this address point at".

addressKnown.description:
`false` when the address is unknown to the history altogether. Absent when the
history does not state it.

block.description: The block the question was asked about.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coverageBlock.description: The highest block the history has been computed up to.

coveredFamilies.description:
Relation ids the history is built for. A relation outside this list is not listed
here whether or not it held.

intervals.description:
The relations that held at `block`, each with its window. `counterpart` is the
object of every relation here.

ReserveLegNow.description: One token of a pool's reserves.

pricingSource.description:
Where the leg's price came from (`observed`, `filled` — carried from an earlier hour —
or `none`) and whether it is trusted, as the source states them.

reserve.description: The reserve in token units, where the decimals are known.

reserveRaw.description:
The reserve as the raw integer, a decimal string (it may be negative where the source
reads a signed balance).

reserveUsd.description: Its USD value, where the token has a price trusted at that size.

symbol.description: The symbol and decimals the token contract declares — verbatim, not verified.

ResolveCorpus.description: A collection a text query is looked up in.

ResolvedBlock.description: A block a number query resolved to. Pass `number` to the block methods.

ResolvedEntity.description: One address the query resolves to.

address.description: The address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Pass it to the address methods.

impersonates.description:
The asset this address is flagged as imitating, by its symbol. Absent when it is not
flagged.

name.description:
The name TraceFast shows for the address — a project, exchange or protocol name, an
ENS name, or the name a contract declares where it is shown. Absent when TraceFast
shows the address under no name.

nameStanding.description:
How TraceFast presents the address: `verified` (confirmed by an official source),
`normal`, `qualified` (shown with a qualifier, e.g. a name the contract declares
about itself), `warning`, `danger` (flagged — for example an impersonation or a
scam), or `unknown`. Other values may be added. Absent when TraceFast holds no
presentation for the address.

token.description: The token contract's own identity, when it is one.

type.description: What kind of address it is.

ResolvedToken.description: The token contract's identity as it declares it.

name.description: The name the contract declares — verbatim, not verified.

state.description:
`found`: TraceFast indexes the address as a token contract, with the name and symbol
below. `absent`: no token metadata is recorded — not a statement that it is no
token. `unavailable`: could not be read for this answer.

symbol.description: The symbol the contract declares — verbatim, not verified.

ResolvedTransaction.description: A transaction a hash query resolved to. Pass `hash` to the transaction methods.

blockNumber.description: The block that includes it, and its index in that block.

ResolvedType.description: What kind of address a match is: its proven type attributes.

attributes.description:
Proven attribute ids of the families `asset` (what it is as an asset, e.g.
`asset:fungible_token`), `address_nature` (e.g. `address_nature:contract_currently`)
and `derived:account_type` — the ones a type is read from; the full set is the
address-attributes method's. Present only when `state` is `known`.

state.description:
`known`: TraceFast has evaluated the address, and `attributes` lists its proven type
attributes (possibly none). `unknown`: not evaluated yet — nothing is denied.
`unavailable`: could not be read for this answer.

Selector.description: One function selector of a contract, resolved to a signature where one is known.

candidateCount.description:
How many known signatures share this selector. `1` is unambiguous; when several do,
`signature` is the most common one.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the resolution is: `partial` (one known signature; parameter names
are not known), `ambiguous` (several known signatures share the selector),
`abi_missing` (no known signature).

name.description:
The function name alone. Present whenever the selector is named; it can be present
WITHOUT `signature` when the only known signature for it is malformed — the name is
served, the malformed text is not.

signature.description:
The canonical signature, for example `transfer(address,uint256)`. Absent when no
known signature has this selector.

SlotEvent.description: One write to a proxy's pointer slot.

kind.description:
`upgrade` — an implementation address was written to the slot (the first one
included); `cleared` — the slot was emptied; `unset` — zero was written, the pointer
removed.

SlotValueChange.description: One block in which the slot's value changed.

valueAfter.description:
The value after the block. Absent when it is not stated (the newest change) — never a
zero standing in.

valueBefore.description: The value before the block, `0x` + 64 hex.

writerTxs.description:
Every transaction that wrote the slot in this block, by position — writes of the value
it already held included. Empty for a system write with no transaction; absent while the
block is not attributed yet.

SlotWriterTx.description: A transaction that wrote the slot.

StateDependency.description:
One read-after-write edge inside a block: `readerTxIndex` read the slot whose last
committed write before it, in this block, was `writerTxIndex`'s.

role.description:
The asked transaction's side: `reader` (it read what an earlier one wrote) or
`writer` (a later one read what it wrote).

StateDependencyPair.description: One pair of dependent transactions, all their shared slots counted.

slots.description: Slots and distinct contracts the pair depends through.

sloadOpcodeTotal.description: SLOAD and SSTORE opcodes executed, reverted frames included.

sloadSlotTouches.description: Distinct slots read and written per transaction, summed over the day.

txsTouching.description: Transactions that touched, read, wrote, and only read (without writing) its storage.

changes.description: Blocks in which its value changed.

currentValue.description: The current value, `0x` + 64 hex — only when `currentValueStatus` is `observed`.

currentValueStatus.description:
`observed`, `system_writes`, `ambiguous_order`, `storage_cleared`,
`no_transaction_write` or `not_computed`. Other values may be added.

StorageWrite.description: One storage slot written by one call frame of a transaction.

callDepth.description: Depth of the writing frame; `1` is the top-level call.

callPath.description:
The writing frame's address in the call tree — the same `callPath` the trace
methods use. Absent when the frame was not recorded.

executionAddress.description:
The address whose code executed the write (differs from `storageAddress` in a
`delegatecall`), and the caller of that frame.

storageAddress.description: The contract whose storage was written.

valueBefore.description:
The value the slot held before this write, 32 bytes. Present only when
`valueBeforeStatus` is `resolved`. A value of all zeroes is a real zero — the slot had
never been written, or had been cleared — not a filler.

valueBeforeStatus.description:
What can be said about the value before: `resolved` (present, and this write's own);
`not_derivable` (it cannot be established for this write and never will be — the
order of writes is not recorded for this block, or the slot is rewritten by a system
call after the transaction); or `not_computed` (the prior value has not been computed
for this write yet — not a statement that the slot was empty. This method refuses a
transaction above the writes' reach with 422 `coverage_gap`, so that is what a caller
normally meets instead).

writeIndex.description:
The execution ordinal of this write within the transaction, where recorded. Writes
are listed in this order; numbers may skip (writes undone by a reverted call are not
listed).

writeIndexStatus.description:
`present`, or `not_recorded` — the order of writes is not known for this block
(blocks below 2675000), which is not the same as "this was write 0".

StorageWriterRow.description: One (caller, execution address) pair that wrote the storage.

callerAddress.description: Who called the frame that wrote.

executionAddress.description: Whose code ran in that frame — the contract itself, or an implementation it delegated to.

uniqueTxs.description: Distinct transactions they happened in — an estimate on large contracts.

Surface.description: Where an interaction can be observed.

Token.description: One token contract, as it declares itself.

decimals.description:
`decimals()` as declared. Absent when the contract declares none (NFTs, and some
fungible tokens) — absent, never a default of 18.

holderCount.description:
Number of addresses holding a positive balance now — the same number the holders
method states. Absent when holders are not covered for this token (every NFT
collection today) — absent, never zero.

holderCountAllTime.description:
Number of distinct addresses that have EVER held the token, including those holding
nothing now. Absent where it is not available for this token.

standard.description:
Token standard as observed from its events: `erc20`, `erc721`, `erc1155`, `erc777`
or `erc4626`; `native` for the chain's own coin.

symbol.description:
`symbol()` and `name()` as the contract declares them — verbatim, not verified.
A contract may declare any text. Absent when the contract declares none.

TokenBalance.description: The balance of one token on one address.

balance.description:
The balance in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. `"0"` is a real zero:
the token is covered and the address holds none of it at `window.asOfBlock`. A token
that is not covered is refused (`token_not_covered`), and a past block with no
recorded balance for the pair is refused too (`balance_not_available`) — never
answered with zero.

decimals.description: Decimals as declared by the token contract; absent when unknown.

symbol.description:
Ticker as declared by the token contract; absent when it declares none. Not a proof
of identity.

TokenClass.description:
Class of token behind a `token` surface. `nft` covers both single- and multi-token
collections; they are not distinguished.

TokenDexVolume.description: A token's daily DEX volume over a window, oldest first.

days.description: The window asked for, in UTC days ending today (today included).

totalSwaps.description: Swaps over the window. Absent when no day is recorded (not the same as zero).

totalVolumeUsd.description:
The USD volume over the window; partial when `unpricedDays` is present. Absent when no
day could be priced.

unpricedDays.description: Days with swaps but no USD price. Absent when there are none.

TokenDexVolumeDay.description: One UTC day of a token's DEX trading.

swapsIn.description: Swaps that sold the token into a pool, and swaps that bought it out of one.

volumeUsd.description: USD volume; absent when the day's swaps could not be priced.

TokenDexVolumeResponse.description: Response of the token DEX volume method.

balance.description:
The balance in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string (not divided by
`decimals`).

TokenHolders.description: The largest current holders of a token.

holderCount.description:
Number of addresses holding a positive balance now — the size of the set this list
is the top of. Holders who once held and now hold nothing are not counted.

holders.description:
Holders in descending balance order, at most `limit` rows. No rank number: balances
can tie, and the order is all the data supports.

compositionStatus.description:
Whether the pool's token list is known, as the source states it (`complete`: every token
of the pool is listed).

creationBlockApprox.description: The block the pool was created around (approximate).

feeTier.description:
The fee tier where the source records one (Uniswap v3 and PancakeSwap v3: hundredths
of a basis point, `500` = 0.05 %). Absent does not mean the pool charges no fee.

pool.description:
The pool contract, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent for a Uniswap v4 pool, which
has no address of its own.

poolId.description:
The pool's own 32-byte id where it has one (the Uniswap v4 PoolId, as the protocol's
events name it). Absent for a pool with an address, and for a v4 pool the pool registry
has not caught up with yet.

protocol.description:
The protocol and its version (`uniswap` / `v3`, `curve`, …); the version is absent
where the protocol has none.

tokens.description: The pool's tokens. Empty when its composition is not known.

volumeUsd7d.description:
USD volume over the last 7 days. Absent when the pool had none that could be priced
(not the same as zero).

TokenPools.description: One page of the pools holding a token, newest created first.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one.

rankedPools.description: How many pools of the token TraceFast ranks (at most the 10 000 most recently created).

TokenPoolsResponse.description: Response of the token pools method.

TokenPrice.description: A token's USD price for one hour.

oneOf.description: The DEX side of the hour; absent when there is none.

divergencePct.description:
How far the oracle and DEX prices disagree, percent, when both exist. A number, not a
verdict.

hour.description: The hour the price is for, Unix seconds (its start).

maxTrustedValueUsd.description:
The largest USD value (amount × `priceUsd`) this price may vouch for. Absent means no
bound. An amount worth more at this price is not valued by it.

observedHour.description: The hour it was observed in, Unix seconds — earlier than `hour` when carried.

oneOf.description: The oracle side of the hour; absent when there is none.

priceSource.description:
What the price is: `chainlink_oracle`, `aave_oracle`, `dex_observed`, `stable_peg`, or
one of them carried over from an earlier hour (`chainlink_carried`,
`aave_oracle_carried`, `dex_carried`).

TokenPriceDex.description: The DEX side of a priced hour: the DEX observation, not the chosen price.

confidenceTier.description: The source's confidence in the DEX price.

pool.description: The pool it came from, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

priceUsd.description: The DEX price of the hour.

pricingRoute.description: How the DEX price was derived, as the source states it.

sourceSwapCount.description: How many swaps and how much USD volume the DEX price stands on.

TokenPriceHistory.description: A token's hourly USD prices over a window, oldest first.

fromHour.description: The window read, as whole hours (Unix seconds, both included).

points.description: Every priced hour in the window; an hour without a price is absent.

TokenPriceHistoryResponse.description: Response of the token price history method.

TokenPriceOracle.description: The oracle side of a priced hour.

address.description: The price feed contract, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

priceUsd.description: The oracle price of the hour; absent when no round landed in it.

roundsInHour.description: Oracle updates within the hour: one is a heartbeat, several mean the price moved.

TokenPricePoint.description: One priced hour of a token.

carried.description: `true` when the price was carried over from an earlier hour.

dexPriceUsd.description: The DEX price and the source's confidence in it, where the hour has one.

divergencePct.description: How far the two disagree, percent, when both exist.

maxTrustedValueUsd.description: The largest USD value this price may vouch for. Absent means no bound.

oraclePriceUsd.description: The oracle price, where a round landed in the hour.

priceSource.description: What the price is (the vocabulary of `getTokenPrice`).

TokenPriceResponse.description: Response of the token price method.

TokenStandardStats.description: Token counts for one token standard.

holderCount.description:
Holder positions: for each token of this standard, the addresses whose received
minus sent transfers is positive now, summed over the tokens — an address holding
three tokens counts three times. Not distinct addresses, and computed from transfer
events rather than balances.

tokenCount.description: Token contracts of this standard with at least one transfer event.

transferCount.description: All-time transfer events of this standard.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

holderCount.description:
Holder positions summed over every standard — see `TokenStandardStats.holderCount`.
Not a number of distinct addresses.

TokenTransfer.description: One transfer event of a token.

batchIndex.description: Position inside an ERC-1155 `TransferBatch`; `0` for every other event.

eventType.description:
`transfer`, `transfer_single`, `transfer_batch`, `sent`, `minted`, `burned`,
`deposit`, `withdraw`, `wrap` or `unwrap`. `deposit` and `withdraw` are vault
(ERC-4626) events; `wrap` and `unwrap` are ether wrapped into and unwrapped from
WETH — one-sided: a `wrap` has no sender, an `unwrap` no recipient.

from.description: Sender of the transfer. Absent on a mint and on a `wrap`.

logIndex.description: The log's index within the block.

operator.description: The operator of an ERC-1155 transfer.

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds. Absent when it could not be resolved.

to.description: Receiver of the transfer. Absent on a burn and on an `unwrap`.

tokenId.description: Token id of an ERC-721 or ERC-1155 transfer, decimal string.

txHash.description:
Hash of the transaction that emitted the transfer. Absent when it could not be
resolved for this page.

txSender.description:
Who sent the transaction that emitted the transfer — on a router or a batch
disburser another party than `from`. Absent when it could not be resolved; never
`from` standing in for it.

txTo.description:
The contract the transaction called at the top level. Absent when it could not be
resolved, or on a contract creation.

value.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, decimal string. Absent on an ERC-721 transfer.

TokenTransfers.description: One page of a token's transfers.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page.

TraceFrame.description: One executed call frame of a transaction.

callPath.description: The frame's address in the tree, and its parent's. Absent parent = the root.

codeAddress.description:
The address whose code this frame runs. On a `delegatecall` this is the
implementation while `to` stays the storage context — the PAIR is what makes a
proxy call readable, which is why `to` does not change meaning. When this address is
an account with an EIP-7702 delegation, the code that ran is its delegate's:
`executedCodeAddress`. Absent where there is no callee code (`create`, `create2`,
`selfdestruct`).

oneOf.description:
The authorization that set that delegation. Present exactly when
`executedCodeAddress` is.

depth.description: Depth in the tree; `1` is the top-level call.

errorSelector.description: The custom error's 4-byte selector — the ERROR selector, not `inputSelector`.

executedCodeAddress.description:
The code that actually ran when `codeAddress` is an account with an EIP-7702
delegation in force at this frame: the delegate the account points at. Present only on
such frames. Where the response's `delegatedCode.status` is `resolved`, a frame without
it ran its own code; while it is `pending`, absence says nothing yet.

gas.description: Gas offered to the frame and gas it consumed, decimal strings.

inputHead.description:
The first 260 bytes of the frame's calldata and of its output, `0x`-hex, with each
full length in BYTES. Present when calldata heads are included: always on the paged
frames, and on the whole trace when `includeCalldata` is true. Compare the size
against 260, not against the hex string's length: the units differ.

order.description:
Position in pre-order traversal of the call tree; `0` is the transaction's own
top-level call.

revertData.description:
The raw ABI revert payload, and its full length in BYTES. The payload may be
truncated, and `revertDataTruncated` says when — a clipped payload decodes into a
plausible but wrong argument list, so the flag is not decoration.

revertDecodeStatus.description:
Why `revertReason` is what it is: `decoded`, `undecodable` (a payload is present
but no name was found) or `absent` (no payload to decode). An empty reason is
ambiguous three ways, and this field is what separates them.

Named apart from the event decoder's `decodeStatus` on purpose: that vocabulary
describes event-decode confidence and the two appear in one response.

revertReason.description: The decoded revert reason, or the custom error's name when its selector is known.

salt.description: `create2` salt, and the keccak-256 of the init code on a creating frame.

selfdestructBeneficiary.description: Who received the balance of a `selfdestruct` frame.

status.description:
`success`, `reverted` or `halted` — the FRAME's own outcome, which on a caught
revert differs from the transaction's.

to.description: The frame's target. Absent on a contract creation.

valueWei.description: Value this frame moved, in wei, as a decimal string.

Transaction.description: One transaction as recorded on chain, with its receipt's outcome.

blockNumber.description: The block that includes it, and the transaction's index within that block.

gasLimit.description: Gas limit and gas used by the receipt, decimal strings.

gasPrice.description:
`gasPrice` as declared (legacy types), `maxFeePerGas` / `maxPriorityFeePerGas`
(EIP-1559), and the price actually PAID per gas — all wei, decimal strings. Each
absent where the type does not carry it; `effectiveGasPrice` absent only while the
block's base fee is not yet available.

hasSelfdestruct.description: Whether a frame ran SELFDESTRUCT. Absent until the trace is computed.

inputSize.description: Size of the input in bytes.

internalTransfersCount.description:
Value transfers made by inner calls, from the call trace. Absent until the trace is
computed (usually within minutes); `0` is a fact.

logCount.description:
Number of receipt logs. Absent where not yet recorded; a log-less transaction is
an honest `0`.

methodId.description:
The first four bytes of the input (`0x`-prefixed), when the input is at least four
bytes long — the function selector of a contract call.

methodName.description:
The called function's name, when its selector is in TraceFast's signature registry
(e.g. `transfer`). Absent when unknown.

oneOf.description:
Why the transaction failed at the top level. Present on a failed transaction once
the trace is computed. Absent otherwise.

revertsTotal.description:
Call frames that reverted, at any depth, from the call trace. A successful
transaction can contain some. Absent until the trace is computed.

status.description:
Receipt status: `1` success, `0` failure. Absent when the receipt is not yet
available — absence is "unknown", never "failed".

oneOf.description:
What the transaction wrote to contract storage. Absent until the storage writes of
its block are computed: a missing block here is "not known yet", never "no writes".

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

to.description: Recipient. Absent for a contract creation.

txType.description: Transaction type (0 legacy, 1 EIP-2930, 2 EIP-1559, 3 EIP-4844, 4 EIP-7702).

TransactionAccountChanges.description:
Every account one transaction changed, with its balance, nonce and code before and after.

Three rules are the source's: the fee recipient has no row when its only change is the
priority fee (so "no row for the fee recipient" does not mean "it did not change"); an
account created and destroyed within the transaction has no row (no net change); the set
is never empty for a computed transaction (its sender always changes).

truncated.description: More accounts than the cap (5 000): these are the first ones by address.

TransactionEvents.description: A page of one transaction's event logs.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

TransactionExecutionProfile.description:
How heavy a transaction was inside the EVM: opcode counts over every frame, the reverted
ones included.

blockNumber.description: The block and the transaction's index in it.

createCount.description: CREATE / CREATE2 frames and SELFDESTRUCT executions, reverted frames included.

delegatecallExecuted.description: At least one DELEGATECALL frame executed, reverted frames included.

distinctStorageAddresses.description: Distinct contracts whose storage the transaction read or wrote.

gasInRevertedFrames.description: Gas spent in frames that reverted, decimal string.

sloadTotal.description:
SLOAD and SSTORE executions. `sstoreTotal` counts executions, reverted frames
included — not the committed writes (`storage.writes` on the transaction).

TransactionFailures.description: Why a transaction reverted, frame by frame.

blockNumber.description: The block that includes it. Absent when there are no failed frames.

frames.description:
Failed call frames, root first, then nested frames in tree order. Empty for a
successful transaction, and for one that is not known — an empty list is "no
failure recorded", never "succeeded".

framesTruncated.description:
`true` when the transaction has more failed frames than this method returns (a
cap of 100); `frames` is then a prefix in tree order.

TransactionFlashLoans.description:
The flash loans taken inside one transaction from the indexed lenders (Aave V2, Balancer
V2, Uniswap V3 flash; Aave V3), in log order. Empty means none from
those lenders — stated
only for a transaction whose block the index has reached; above it the method answers 422,
never an empty list.

TransactionFrames.description: A page of one transaction's call frames in pre-order.

delegatedCode.description: Whether `executedCodeAddress` is decided for this transaction's frames.

frames.description:
This page. `order` on each frame is its position in the whole tree, so a page
starting at `order` 50 continues the one that ended at 49.

framesTruncated.description:
`true` on the last page when the tree is larger than the 20 000 frames this method
walks and frames remain unserved. A clipped tree never claims to be the whole one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

TransactionLiquidityEvents.description: The liquidity events of a transaction.

TransactionLiquidityEventsResponse.description: Response of the transaction liquidity events method.

TransactionRevert.description: The top-level failure of a transaction.

data.description: The raw revert payload, `0x`-prefixed. It may be cut: see `dataTruncated`.

dataSize.description: The payload's full size in bytes.

errorSelector.description: The custom error's selector (the first four bytes of the revert payload), `0x`-prefixed.

kind.description:
The kind of failure: `Revert`, `Panic`, `CustomError`, `OutOfGas`, `StackOverflow`,
`InvalidOpcode`, `PrecompileError`, `Other`, or `Unknown(<n>)` — the same vocabulary as
the failures method. Other values may be added.

reason.description:
The reason as the contract states it: the message of `Error(string)`, the panic code,
or the custom error's name when its selector is known. It is text written by the
contract's author. Absent when it cannot be decoded.

TransactionStateDependencies.description:
Which other transactions of its block a transaction depends on through storage, and
which depend on it. Facts of execution order only: no verdict about intent.

pairs.description: The same, folded per pair of transactions.

pairsComplete.description: `false` when the pairs were folded from a clipped edge list.

truncated.description: More edges than the cap: these are the first ones.

TransactionStorage.description: What a transaction wrote to contract storage.

TransactionStorageWrites.description: A page of one transaction's storage writes.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

writes.description: This page, in call-tree order: by the writing frame, then by slot.

writesTruncated.description:
`true` on the last page when the transaction wrote more than the 5 000 slots this
method serves and writes remain unserved.

TransactionTrace.description: The call tree of one transaction, in pre-order.

delegatedCode.description: Whether `executedCodeAddress` is decided for this transaction's frames.

frameCount.description: Frames in this response. Equal to the tree's size unless `framesTruncated`.

framesTruncated.description:
`true` when the tree holds more frames than this response — past the `limit` asked
for, or past the 1 000-frame cap — and this is its first `frameCount` frames in the
order they ran. A clipped tree never claims to be the whole one.

totalFrameCount.description:
Frames in the WHOLE tree, whatever `limit` asked for — so a small `limit` still
says how large the trace is. Absent when the tree is larger than the 1 000-frame
cap: its size is then not known here, only that it exceeds the cap.

TransactionTransientWrites.description:
The committed transient writes of a transaction, in execution order. Empty for a computed
transaction means "no transient writes".

truncated.description: More writes than the cap (5 000): these are the first ones.

TransferToken.description:
The token a transfer moved, as the contract declares itself. Same words as the token
method; no price and no name from any resolver.

address.description: The token contract. It is what identifies the token — the symbol and the name do not.

decimals.description:
Declared decimals. Absent when the contract declares none — never a default `18`,
which would silently misprice every amount.

name.description: The name as the contract declares it; self-declared, like `symbol`.

symbol.description:
The symbol as the contract DECLARES it. Anyone can deploy a token that calls itself
`ETH` or `USDT`: a symbol here is not a statement that the token is the well-known
one. Check the address.

TransientWrite.description: One committed TSTORE (EIP-1153; none before block 19 426 976).

callDepth.description: The frame's depth, 1 = the top-level call.

callPath.description: The writing frame's path, as on the trace and storage-write methods (join by this).

callerAddress.description: The caller of the writing frame.

executionAddress.description: The code that executed the TSTORE (differs from `storageAddress` under DELEGATECALL).

storageAddress.description: The contract whose transient storage was written.

storageKey.description: The slot and the value written.

writeIndex.description: The write's order in the transaction. Absent where it is not numbered.

TxLiquidityEvent.description: One liquidity event of a transaction.

action.description: `add` or `remove`, and the event as the pool names it.

logIndex.description: The event's index in the block.

pool.description: The pool, its protocol and version.

pricedLegs.description: The event's token legs that could and could not be priced.

provider.description: The liquidity provider the event names, where it names one.

TxLiquidityLeg.description: One token leg of a liquidity event in a transaction.

amountRaw.description:
The amount, raw (a decimal string) and in token units where the decimals are known,
and whether it went into the pool or out of it.

amountUsd.description:
Its USD value and the price behind it, where it could be priced, and how it was
valued, as the source states it.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: what a reference means. An address (`0x` + 40 hex) is described — the name TraceFast shows for it, how it presents it, what kind of address it is, its token identity. Any other text is looked up in two collections — token contracts by the symbol and name they declare, and the names TraceFast shows for projects, exchanges, protocols and ENS names — and answered with the matching addresses, best first: verified addresses, then the projects and ENS names TraceFast knows by name (flagged ones included), then the rest, and impersonations last — never hidden; inside each group exact, then prefix, then substring matches, then tokens with more holders. Decoding covers the common token, DeFi and protocol events; an unknown signature is returned raw with `decodeStatus: abi_missing`, and a known one whose layout does not fit the log with `failed` — raw as well, without `decoded`.
